rules.output: Docker packages an application and its dependencies into a container image that runs the same way on any machine. Build an image with `docker build`, start it with `docker run`.

# What Docker is
Docker is a platform for building and running applications in containers: isolated processes that share the host kernel but ship with their own filesystem and dependencies.

## Images and containers
An image is a read-only template built from a Dockerfile. A container is a running instance of an image.

## Example
```Dockerfile
FROM node:22-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY . .
RUN npm ci
CMD ["node", "server.js"]
```
Build it with `docker build -t my-api .` and run it with `docker run -p 3000:3000 my-api`.

## Why it matters
The same image runs identically on a laptop, in CI and in production, which removes most environment drift.

# What Docker is
Docker is a platform for packaging applications into containers, which are isolated processes bundled with their own filesystem and dependencies.

## Images and containers
You describe an environment in a Dockerfile and build it into an image. Running an image creates a container.

## Why it matters
Containers behave the same on every machine, so builds are reproducible and deployments are predictable.
